patch.value: pm rl lineage promises invalidation state in its own help text but renders none, so a generation trained on an invalidated environment still reads as a clean promotion candidate

value.author: claude
value.text:
Found 2026-08-29 by exercising the full recursive-self-improvement lifecycle against a scratch workspace with the real examples/ fixtures, using pm 2026.8.28 with pm-rl installed from this working tree.

WHAT WORKS, verified end to end. Environment registration is content-addressed (grid-world.json to pm-env-grid-world-3-f18722ed5451). Run lifecycle start, log, finish behaves (3 metrics appended from examples/metrics.ndjson, status closed). Generation registration records a genuine lineage edge: gen1 came back with seed:false, parent:pm-gen0, collection_runs:[pm-ppo-seed-001], environment, spec_hash and reward_spec_version. Transitive invalidation reports correctly with a path: invalidating the environment listed pm-ppo-seed-001 as a Run at 1 hop, reached by env to run. The refusal when I aimed invalidate at a Generation is CORRECT and well-worded: invalidation starts from an environment or benchmark version because changing a generation invalidates no tracked result.

THE GAP. 'pm rl lineage --help' describes itself as:

  lineage [options] [head]   Render the generation chain from seed to head(s)
                             with promotion evidence and invalidation state.

It renders no invalidation state. After invalidating pm-env-grid-world-3-f18722ed5451 (which pm rl invalidate confirms transitively reaches pm-ppo-seed-001, the exact run listed in gen1's collection_runs), lineage still prints:

  pm-gen0 | seed       | base=sha256-aaa000 | runs=              | ... | candidate
  pm-gen1 | generation | base=sha256-bbb111 | runs=pm-ppo-seed-001 | ... | candidate

Both still read 'candidate'. There is no invalidation column in the table, and --format json contains no key matching /invalid/ anywhere in the document. So the one view whose stated job is to show invalidation state is the view that does not show it.

WHY THIS MATTERS AND IS NOT COSMETIC. This is the core safety property of the RSI story. pm rl invalidate is deliberately a read-only LIST (its help says 'List every Run, EvalResult and Transfer transitively invalidated'), so it changes no state by design and that is fine. But that makes lineage the only place a reviewer would ever see contamination. Today a generation whose training data came from a run reached by an invalidated environment version is indistinguishable from a clean one, and remains a promotable candidate. Recursive self-improvement is exactly the setting where a contaminated ancestor must not silently propagate down the chain.

Note the ingredients for the fix are already present: gen1 stores collection_runs, environment and reward_spec_version, and the invalidate resolver already computes transitive reachability with paths. lineage needs to run that same reachability from each row's environment and collection_runs and mark the row.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Add an invalidation column to the table and a corresponding field in the JSON view, populated from the existing invalidate reachability. A generation should surface at least: whether its environment version is invalidated, and whether any of its collection_runs is transitively reached. Consider refusing promotion of a generation in that state, since promotion already requires an approval decision and separate proxy and held-out scores, and this is the same class of guard.

TEST NOTE. A regression test for this must fail on revert. Assert that after invalidating the environment, lineage marks gen1, and confirm the assertion fails against the current implementation before the fix lands.
